newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firm, DBS foreign recovers.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firm, DBS foreign recovers.

text.p: Singapore shares were firm at the open on Thursday and DBS foreign shares rebounded ahead of the release of the bank's results after the market close later today.
Dealers said sentiment was steady partly because of the strong rally on Wall Street overnight.
"Market is firm. But some stocks are facing resistances as prices aren't cheap," said a local broker.
DBS foreign shares were up 30 Singapore cents (US$0.21) to S$18.10. Dealers said there was some concern over the bank's exposure to troubled Thai banks.
At 0120 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrial index was up 1.75 points at 2,194.28 while the UOB OTC index for mostly Malaysian issues was up 3.99 at 1,333.96.
Total market volume was over 86 million units with 194 gainers overwhelming 43 losers. Among the most actives was newly listed mould maker Omni Industries which was down one cent to S$0.75.
Amtek rose 14 cents to S$2.85. A broker said some houses have recommended a buy on it. "It had fallen quite sharply recently." Losers include Sembawang Corp and Hai Sun Hup Group.
